messages:
liam: hey all, newcomer question — I can start postgres in compose but my app (running in another compose service) intermittently fails with "could not translate host name "db" to address: Temporary failure in name resolution". sometimes a restart fixes it. any ideas?

ara: welcome! that error sounds like DNS resolution flakiness on docker network. are you using compose v2+ and multiple project names or launching parts separately?

liam: i run `docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml up db -d` then `docker-compose up app` in another terminal. i think both use same file.

jin: when you start services separately, Docker may create separate networks if the project name differs. try `docker-compose up` (both services) so they share the same network, or ensure the same `-p` project flag. Also `docker network ls` and `docker inspect <network>` to confirm.

liam: oh interesting — i was using my laptop hostname in an env script for the app earlier which set COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME to `liam-dev` and then later used plain compose which generated `compose_default`. that could do it?

ara: yep. different project names => different networks => service name `db` won't resolve across them. Pick one project name or run everything together. For quick fix: connect the app container to the db network: `docker network connect <db_network> <app_container>` but better to keep compose consistent.

jin: also if you see transient DNS failures, check if your machine is low on resources; docker's embedded DNS may fail when the daemon restarts. `docker-compose logs` and `docker ps` timeline helps.

liam: consolidated into one `docker-compose up` and removed my custom COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME. reconnects reliably now. thanks!

devex-bot: pinned tips: 1) keep a single compose project for local stacks to avoid multiple networks 2) prefer service names (db) not localhost when app in compose 3) use `docker-compose ps`/`docker network inspect` to debug name resolution. internal doc: https://redwood.internal/dev/compose-networks
